comment: The register of which repos are frozen and why. Kept here, in MAM-basics, rather than as a marker file inside each frozen repo: writing such a marker would itself change the repo and destroy the very last-changed date the freeze exists to preserve. Deliberately separate from in/vendoring_policy.json, whose per-repo 'ignore' flag means 'do not scan this repo for vendoring' -- a different question from 'do not touch this repo at all'. The lists are not the same one: CCAR-Psalms is frozen here and is not ignored there, so neither may be derived from the other.
location_comment: Ben's decision, 2026-08-07: the frozen clones no longer live in GitRepos. They were moved to C:\Users\BenDe\FrozenRepos, a sibling of GitRepos, and dropped from all-repos.code-workspace, which went from 30 folders to 24. THE FREEZE IS THEREFORE STRUCTURAL NOW, NOT ADVISORY: every sweep in py/main_repo_util.py iterates the repos a workspace file lists and resolves them under --repos-root, so no action can reach a frozen repo at all -- not just --run-black, which was the only action consulting this list (open issue #211). Two consequences worth knowing. First, this file no longer skips anything at run time, because there is nothing left for it to skip; it is documentation, and the location does the work. Second, a frozen repo is no longer swept for leftover agent worktrees either, which is fine while nothing runs sessions in FrozenRepos, and is the thing to revisit if that ever changes. To thaw a repo, move its clone back into GitRepos, re-add it to all-repos.code-workspace, and delete its entry here.

CCAR-Psalms.comment: Paused client project. Not among the repos in/vendoring_policy.json ignores, which is why that flag cannot stand in for this list.

MAM-for-CCAR.comment: Paused client project. Note this one was six months rather than years old when frozen, so its last-changed date only starts testifying to the pause from here.

mamgo-auto-edits.comment: Archived on GitHub, so the remote is READ-ONLY and no maintenance commit can ever land: a push returns 403, 'This repository was archived so it is read-only'. Found 2026-08-07 the hard way, by a .gitattributes standardization commit that had to be dropped again because it could not be pushed. Archived-on-GitHub and frozen-here nearly coincide -- the five repos above are all archived too -- but neither list may be derived from the other, and 2026-08-07 showed both edges at once: this repo was archived and not frozen, while breuer-cos was frozen and deliberately NOT archived, so that its issues stay writable.

TMC.comment: Paused project, frozen alongside the MAM-for-* client repos.
